what: The input-only rule's cost, measured on real Tier 2 checkpoints: 0.062 AUC on one clip
measured: 2026-10-30 06:23 UTC, e29's seven surviving second-wave checkpoints
what_the_rule_did: Four checkpoints have no drop. The rule takes the lowest input error, which is 349,999,104 at 3.06 cm, scoring 0.56478. The truth-optimal choice is 199,999,488 at 3.16 cm, scoring 0.62687. The rule discriminated on a 0.10 cm difference and surrendered 0.062 of AUC.
why_this_is_more_than_a_curiosity: It is the physics-correction hypothesis (results/t2_physics_correction_idea.json) measured on real data. More training fits the NOISY reference better -- input error falls 3.16 -> 3.06 cm -- and fits truth worse, AUC 0.627 -> 0.565. On Tier 2 the reference is corrupted, so tracking it harder is actively wrong past some point, and the input-only rule rewards exactly that.
a_legal_refinement_with_a_mechanism: Among no-drop checkpoints whose input error is within a margin of the minimum, prefer the EARLIEST rather than the lowest. That reads no truth, so it stays legal on Tier 2 and Tier 3, and it has a mechanism: later checkpoints have had more opportunity to fit the noise. On this clip it would pick 199,999,488 and gain +0.062. This is the same shape as the 2% margin added for Tier 3, where a 0.56% input gain was noise.
how_far_it_might_go: If a 0.062 gain were typical of clips whose no-drop checkpoints tie within ~0.1 cm, and a third of the 30 clips tie that way, the entry mean would rise about +0.02 -- which is more than the +0.0155 that separates us from 4th on tier2-auc. That is a rank point, from selection alone, with no training.
why_it_cannot_be_tested_now: The other clips' per-checkpoint rollouts were deleted in the disk cleanup that kept us above the 20 GB floor; only e29's seven survived. Re-generating them is evaluation-only -- no training -- at roughly $0.05 per checkpoint of GPU, so about $4.50 for 30 clips x 7 checkpoints. That is the cheapest credible rank point left anywhere on the board, and it is cheaper than every training arm.
what_i_did_not_do: I did not adopt the 200M checkpoint for e29. It would be truth-based selection against the registered rule, worth +0.00207 on the entry mean and no rank change. The finding is worth more than the 0.002, and taking it would have made the finding unusable as evidence.

CORRECTION_06_25.what_i_got_wrong: I wrote that testing the earliest-checkpoint rule is 'EVALUATION ONLY, ~$4.50 for 30 clips x 7 checkpoints -- the cheapest credible rank point left anywhere'. That is wrong by a factor of twenty, and it was the headline of the claim.
CORRECTION_06_25.why: Evaluating a checkpoint needs the checkpoint's WEIGHTS. ship_ckpts_wave2 holds exactly one policy per clip -- policy_349999104, the final -- because that is all the second-wave pullers brought home. The intermediate weights lived on boxes that were deleted. What survives for e29 is seven already-evaluated ROLLOUTS, not seven policies, and a rollout cannot be re-evaluated into a different clip's answer.
CORRECTION_06_25.the_real_cost: Getting intermediate checkpoints for the other 29 clips means RETRAINING them, which is the full 30-clip run at about $90 -- the most expensive arm on the board, not the cheapest. The finding stands; its price does not.
CORRECTION_06_25.what_is_actually_cheap: Nothing, for this rule, on existing data. The one affordable version is to apply it to arms we run in FUTURE: run_tier2_full.sh already evaluates every checkpoint, so any funded run should pull every checkpoint's rollout rather than only the final, and then the earliest-within-margin rule can be applied for free at pack time.
CORRECTION_06_25.the_avoidable_part: Those per-checkpoint rollouts DID exist for all 30 clips and I deleted them myself in the disk cleanup that kept us above the 20 GB floor. They are the raw material for every selection-rule question, they are small compared with the policies, and I kept the policies instead. If a future session has the choice, keep the rollouts.

status: Finding: measured and sound on one clip. Price: corrected from $4.50 to ~$90, so it is no longer the cheapest rank point and should NOT be funded ahead of T1XFER ($10) or the Tier 2 physics test ($1.50). Its cheap form is a change to how future runs are pulled.

the_free_fix_for_future_runs.what: A 50M-step warm start at the stock save interval of 49,999,872 produces exactly ONE checkpoint, so the earliest-within-margin rule has nothing to choose between. At a 2048-aligned interval of 9,999,872 the same run produces FIVE.
the_free_fix_for_future_runs.cost: No extra training at all -- the steps are identical. Four more evaluations per clip at 1-2 min each is about $0.06 to $0.11 per clip at $0.68/h, plus a little disk.
the_free_fix_for_future_runs.applied_to: SAVE_EVERY=9999872 is now set in the staged T1WEAK launcher's BOX_ENV. The arm currently running (e19) started with the stock interval and cannot be changed mid-flight -- editing a script a runner is reading is what cost clip e29 once already -- so it will yield one checkpoint and the rule will not apply to it.
the_free_fix_for_future_runs.why_it_matters: It converts a finding that costs $90 to test retrospectively into one that is free prospectively: any funded run from here produces the checkpoints the rule needs, and the choice is then made at pack time for nothing.
